name: dev.ucp.common.feed
title: Feed
description: A feed is a point-in-time publication of records—each representing one logical data item—delivered in bulk as files. Records normally use a UCP-defined shape from a service or capability, so a Platform can discover them in bulk, then call corresponding live operations for authoritative serving-time values. A Business MAY publish feeds using a custom record shape through a record-type extension negotiated with the Platform, and MAY publish feeds without corresponding live operations. Common Feed adds one endpoint declaration, a feed list, and a manifest; it defines no record model. The manifest's ucp.capabilities declares the record type, defined by an extension of Common Feed. The Business declares a feed endpoint in the capability `config`; a Platform fetches the feed list document from it, then fetches each feed's manifest and files. For every record type, including custom record types, the Business MUST use stable entity identifiers that it can resolve in related operations. The record-type specification defines which identifiers corresponding operations accept and what they identify. Where those operations are advertised, the Business MUST resolve those identifiers to the same entities. Publishing a feed does not require advertising those operations.

endpoint.description: Absolute HTTPS URL from which a Platform fetches the feed list. The operator of this endpoint acts for the Business and may be the Business, its commerce platform, or a delegated feed publisher; the Business declares it in its profile.

platform_schema.title: Feed Capability (Platform)
platform_schema.description: Platform-level feed capability declaration. Platforms advertise that they consume feeds; the feed endpoint is business-specific, so no platform config is required.

business_schema.title: Feed Capability (Business)
business_schema.description: Business declaration for the feed endpoint.

response_schema.title: Feed Capability (Response)
response_schema.description: Feed capability reference in feed documents.

feed_list.description: The feed list document served at the capability's `config.endpoint`: the feeds the Business makes available to the calling Platform.

feeds.description: Feeds available to the calling Platform. May be empty. The document is provisioned for the caller: an unauthenticated fetch returns the Business's public feeds, if any; an authenticated fetch returns the feeds the Business has provisioned for that Platform. The order of entries carries no meaning, except that a Platform applies supplemental feeds of the same base feed in list order.

messages.description: Errors, warnings, or informational messages about the feed list.

feed.description: A feed list entry: the Business's advertisement of one feed and a pointer to its current snapshot. The entry is for discovery; the manifest is authoritative.

id.description: Business-assigned, stable identifier for the feed. Opaque to Platforms; unique within the Business's feed list. Identifies the feed across snapshots: `generated_at` advances, `id` does not.

context.description: The conditions under which every record in the feed was resolved, each member single-valued. The capability that defines the feed's records states which members its feeds use and what each means. For a supplemental feed, the context of the composed result: the base feed with this feed applied.

format.description: Specification-defined namespaced format identifier for a concrete record-type representation profile, covering every file in the feed's current snapshot. The format MUST be defined by a record-type or other extension declared in the manifest's `ucp.capabilities`. The Business MUST set the feed list entry's `format` and the `format` in the manifest referenced by that entry's `manifest` URL to the same value. The manifest is authoritative. A Platform that fetches the manifest and finds that these values differ MUST NOT consume the snapshot. Lets a Platform select feeds it can read, and skip ones it cannot, without fetching manifests. A Platform MUST use the full identifier when determining format support, MUST NOT infer a decoder from its suffix, and MUST NOT consume a snapshot with an unrecognized or unsupported format.

interval.description: Expected cadence between snapshots as an ISO 8601 duration (RFC 3339 Appendix A), e.g. `P1D`, `PT2H`. A positive duration. Advisory: it states the Business's intent, not a guarantee. Platforms are expected to poll no more often than the shortest interval among the feeds they consume unless the Business agrees otherwise.

generated_at.description: Copy of the current manifest's `generated_at`. Strictly increasing per feed. A Platform compares it with the value of the snapshot it holds to decide whether to fetch the manifest.

manifest.description: Absolute HTTPS URL of the feed's current manifest. Each snapshot has its own manifest URL, and the document at a manifest URL does not change once published. It may be on any HTTPS origin; it is trusted because the feed list obtained from the Business's declared `config.endpoint` returned it.

extends.description: `id` of the base feed this supplemental feed extends: another entry in this feed list that itself carries no `extends`. Present only for a supplemental feed, whose records are applied to the base records with the same `id`. Absent for a feed that stands alone.

manifest.description: The document at a feed entry's `manifest` URL: a complete materialization of one feed as of `generated_at`. Identified by (`id`, `generated_at`); once published, neither the manifest document nor its files change, and a correction is a new snapshot with a later `generated_at`. The manifest is authoritative; the feed list entry is for discovery.

ucp.description: Declares the UCP version and the capabilities, including extensions, whose schemas the records in this snapshot conform to. Same envelope as a UCP response.

id.description: The feed's identifier. Equals the `id` of the feed list entry whose `manifest` URL served this document.

format.description: Specification-defined namespaced format identifier for a concrete record-type representation profile covering every file in `files`, not a generic encoding label. Its defining specification describes record layout, serialization, and compression. Open reverse-domain vocabulary. Common Feed defines no universal format values or decoder-support obligation. The Business MUST use a format defined by a record-type or other extension declared in this manifest's `ucp.capabilities`. A Platform MUST use the full identifier when determining format support, MUST NOT infer a decoder from its suffix, and MUST NOT consume a snapshot with an unrecognized or unsupported format or one not defined by an extension declared in this manifest. Record conformance remains declared by `ucp.capabilities`. The Business MUST set the feed list entry's `format` and the `format` in the manifest referenced by that entry's `manifest` URL to the same value. The manifest is authoritative. A Platform that fetches the manifest and finds that these values differ MUST NOT consume the snapshot.

context.description: Equals the feed list entry's `context`; the manifest is authoritative. The conditions under which every record in the feed was resolved, each member single-valued. The capability that defines the feed's records states which members its feeds use and what each means. For a supplemental feed, the context of the composed result: the base feed with this feed applied.

extends.description: Equals the feed list entry's `extends`: the `id` of the base feed this supplemental feed extends, an entry that itself carries no `extends`. Present only for a supplemental feed, whose records are applied to the base records with the same `id`.

generated_at.description: Logical point in time of the snapshot. Every file in the manifest is consistent as of this instant. Strictly increasing per feed; equals the feed list entry's `generated_at` for the current snapshot.

expires_at.description: Time after which the Business no longer guarantees that the manifest and its files remain retrievable. Retention, not validity: a snapshot does not become wrong at `expires_at`; it may become unavailable.

files.description: Flat list of the files that together make up this snapshot; a single file is a one-element list. All files are mutually consistent as of `generated_at`, and the Business publishes every file before publishing the manifest that references it. A Platform that cannot retrieve every file does not treat the snapshot as complete.

messages.description: Errors, warnings, or informational messages about this snapshot.

file.description: One file in a snapshot. Encoded per the manifest's `format`.

url.description: Location of the file: an absolute HTTPS URL, or a reference relative to the manifest's URL. May be on any origin.

digest.description: RFC 9530 `Content-Digest` dictionary value for the file's bytes as served, e.g. `sha-256=:BASE64:`. Same syntax UCP uses for `Content-Digest` in signing. Optional but recommended. Verifies the file bytes against this manifest; it is not a signature and does not establish who published the file. A Platform that verifies and finds a mismatch treats the snapshot as incomplete.
